title: trio of men emerges from sewer box near Penn Station
seoTitle: Trio Emerges From NYC Sewer Near Penn Station
subtitle: police investigate video of people excavating in the city's sewer network
excerpt: A TikTok video shows three men in work pants and headlamps emerging from a Manhattan sewer box near Penn Station just after 4 a.m.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
A video posted on TikTok shows three men in work pants and headlamps emerging from a Manhattan sewer box near Penn Station just after 4 a.m. Police are investigating the case, with no arrests made, and confirm there is no damage to the infrastructure.

how the video surfaced

The video was posted on May 6 and shows the men emerging from the sewer box located at 32nd Street and 7th Avenue, near Penn Station and Madison Square Garden. The person who posted the video reported that the incident occurred after 4 a.m. on Tuesday.

ongoing investigation

The NYPD confirmed that it is aware of the video and that the investigation is ongoing. No arrests have been made yet, and police dispatched Emergency Service Unit officers to check that nothing dangerous was left behind by the individuals.

safety and infrastructure damage

The city's Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an inspection of the sewer system near the location and reported that there was no damage to the infrastructure. The DEP emphasized that entering sewers is "both illegal and extremely dangerous," highlighting the risks of toxic gases, unstable surfaces, flood hazards, and confined spaces.

possible motivation of those involved

In previous investigations into similar incidents in Brooklyn and Williamsburg, the main theory was that individuals were searching for valuables that ended up in the sewer system. The same hypothesis is being considered for the recent video.

context of similar incidents

Videos of men emerging from sewer boxes in different parts of the city circulated online in May. In one case, a man lifted a sewer box cover in Brooklyn, allowing seven men to emerge and change clothes on a busy street. In another, seven men emerged from a sewer box on Bedford Avenue, some carrying shovels. In both cases, police concluded there was no immediate threat to the public and that the sewer system remained intact.

With information from NBC News, New York Post.
